data.title: Example: lecture excerpt
data.content: Photosynthesis has two stages. The light reactions capture energy from sunlight in the thylakoid membranes, producing ATP and NADPH. The Calvin cycle then uses that energy in the stroma to fix carbon dioxide into sugar.

data.title: Light reactions vs. Calvin cycle
data.content: Capture energy, then spend it to build sugar. The plant's energy pipeline.

data.title: Why does the Calvin cycle depend on light?
data.content: If light disappears, how long can the Calvin cycle run on stored ATP and NADPH?

data.title: "Plants only photosynthesize, never respire"
data.content: I used to think plants don't do cellular respiration. They do, constantly.

data.rationale: The excerpt describes both stages; this concept compresses it.
If one stage feeds the other, removing light should stall the second.
